subject.title: fix(memory): search memory and wiki concurrently for corpus=all (#92633)

question: Should this PR close the canonical all-corpus timeout issue when it lands, or should the closing reference be narrowed so timeout attribution/debug follow-up remains open?
rationale: The PR appears correct for the additive-latency root cause, but the linked issue also asks for warning/debug attribution that is owned by a separate open PR, so automation cannot choose the issue-closure boundary for maintainers.

options.title: Narrow Closure Before Merge
options.body: Change the closing wording or add maintainer direction so this PR lands the concurrency fix without automatically closing the diagnostic follow-up.

options.title: Accept Scoped Closure
options.body: Treat this concurrency fix as sufficient to close the central issue and keep attribution/debug work in the adjacent PR as independent follow-up.

options.title: Pause For Coordination
options.body: Hold this PR until maintainers decide whether both linked fixes should land together or in a specific order.

recommendation.title: Narrow Closure Before Merge
recommendation.body: Change the closing wording or add maintainer direction so this PR lands the concurrency fix without automatically closing the diagnostic follow-up.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc is the strongest history signal for the memory-wiki corpus bridge and current supplement behavior touched by the PR.
